evidence: backend/crates/api-core/src/middleware/tenant_filter.rs:14 — `tenant_filter` is a dead, stubbed tenant-isolation middleware that is MISLEADING rather than merely unused. It is exported (`middleware/mod.rs:9 pub mod tenant_filter; :18 pub use tenant_filter::*;`) but wired into NO router: a repo-wide grep for `tenant_filter(` outside its own definition returns zero hits (the real RLS/tenant enforcement is the `RlsConnection` extractor, referenced in 108 route files under servers/api-server/src/routes, plus the host-based `ResolvedTenant` resolver). The function's own body (`:30`-`:36`) documents the three validations it is SUPPOSED to perform — `// 1. Tenant exists and is active // 2. User has access to this tenant // 3. Rate limiting per tenant` — and implements NONE of them: on the `Some(_id)` arm it simply runs the request (`Ok(next.run(request).await)`), so any caller presenting a well-formed (but otherwise unverified, client-supplied, spoofable) `X-Tenant-ID` header passes. As dead code today it is harmless, but it is a security-shaped trap: its name, doc-comment (`:12`-`:13` "ensure tenant isolation" / "Validates ... X-Tenant-ID"), and TODO list invite a future developer to `.layer()` it believing it enforces tenant isolation, when it neither validates DB membership nor cross-checks the header against the authenticated JWT principal — exactly the IDOR class that issue #1525 already had to remediate elsewhere (servers/api-server/src/routes/integrations/sync.rs:151-160). Severity LOW (+1): not reachable in production (unwired), so this is a maintenance-hazard / latent-security-trap tech-debt finding, not a live auth bypass — hence confidence medium (statically confirmed unwired; cannot rule out a future wiring). NET-NEW vs backlog: no open code-review-finding row references tenant_filter or rls_context (the only backlog hit, code-review-api-handlers-compliance-superadmin-exact-match, is a distinct done api-handlers item). Suggested cloud-landable fix (backend-only, verifiable with `cargo clippy` dead-code lint + a router wiring test): DELETE `tenant_filter` + `tenant_logging` and their `pub use` (preferred — they duplicate functionality the `RlsConnection` extractor + `host_tenant`/`TenantExtractor` already own); or, if retained, gate them behind `#[deprecated]` + a doc note that they are NOT an isolation boundary and must not be layered.

backend/crates/api-core/src/middleware/rls_context.rs:70 — `rls_context_middleware` (and its stricter sibling `require_rls_context` at `:185`) is dead code AND, if ever wired, would set an incorrect RLS tenant scope for host/subdomain-based clients. (a) Dead: a repo-wide grep for `rls_context_middleware`/`require_rls_context` outside their definitions returns zero call sites; lib.rs wires `security_headers`, `TraceLayer`, CORS, and state/extension layers but never this middleware. The live RLS enforcement is the per-connection `RlsConnection` extractor (108 route references), which sets the Postgres GUCs on the SAME pooled connection the handler then queries. (b) Latent correctness gap: this middleware derives the tenant ONLY from the `X-Tenant-ID` header (`:87`-`:91` `.get("X-Tenant-ID")...Uuid::parse_str`), but the authoritative tenant source has since moved to the host-resolved `ResolvedTenant` extension — see extractors/tenant.rs:44-60, whose own doc states the host-resolved tenant "is authoritative" and the `X-Tenant-ID` header is the LEGACY fallback. So a request arriving via host/subdomain tenant resolution (no `X-Tenant-ID` header) reaches `:106 let should_set_rls = user_id.is_some() || tenant_id.is_some();` with `tenant_id = None`, and if `user_id` is present it calls `set_request_context(pool, None, user_id, ...)` (`:110`-`:116`) — i.e. it would install an RLS context whose org scope is NULL for exactly the modern subdomain clients, silently widening/disabling org-scoping at the DB layer for those requests were this middleware ever activated. It also acquires/sets context on a pooled connection separate from the one the handler later borrows (`set_request_context(pool.as_ref(), ...)`), so the GUCs would not even apply to the handler's query — a second reason it cannot be a correct substitute for `RlsConnection`. Severity LOW (+1): unreachable today (unwired), so maintenance-hazard tech-debt rather than a live isolation break — confidence medium (statically traced; dead-code + source-of-truth divergence confirmed, production impact contingent on a future wiring). NET-NEW vs backlog: no open finding references rls_context. Suggested cloud-landable fix (backend-only, verifiable with `cargo clippy` dead-code lint): DELETE `rls_context_middleware` + `require_rls_context` (the `RlsConnection` extractor is the single source of truth); or, if a global pre-handler RLS layer is genuinely wanted, rewrite it to read `ResolvedTenant` first (header only as legacy fallback) AND set the GUCs on the handler's own connection, then add a wiring + cross-tenant regression test before layering it.
